claim: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a functional gastro-intestinal disorder affecting 3–5% of adults in industrial countries.
source: As defined by the Rome IV criteria, irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a functional gastro-intestinal disorder affecting 3–5% of adults in industrial countries.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to established diagnostic criteria (Rome IV) and represents established knowledge about IBS prevalence.

claim: IBS results in various symptoms that strongly affect the patients' quality of life.
source: IBS results in various symptoms that strongly affect the patients' quality of life (Dean et al., 2005) and a significant socioeconomic burden (Peery et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dean et al., 2005 and Peery et al., 2012.

claim: IBS results in a significant socioeconomic burden.
source: IBS results in various symptoms that strongly affect the patients' quality of life (Dean et al., 2005) and a significant socioeconomic burden (Peery et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Peery et al., 2012.

claim: Abdominal pain is a prevalent IBS symptom, associated with changes in bowel habits (diarrhoea and/or constipation).
source: Abdominal pain is a prevalent IBS symptom, associated with changes in bowel habits (diarrhoea and/or constipation; Camilleri et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Camilleri et al., 2012.

claim: IBS symptoms may originate from peripheral and/or central mechanisms resulting in a dysfunctional gut-brain axis.
source: Even though IBS pathophysiology remains not completely understood, IBS symptoms may originate from peripheral and/or central mechanisms resulting in a dysfunctional gut-brain axis (Fichna and Storr, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Fichna and Storr, 2012.

claim: Anxiety and stressful psychological life events lead to central nervous system (CNS) disorder triggering in turn gut motility dysfunctions.
source: Anxiety and stressful psychological life events lead to central nervous system (CNS) disorder triggering in turn gut motility dysfunctions (Mönnikes et al., 2001) and strengthen visceral sensitivity (Greenwood-Van Meerveld et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Mönnikes et al., 2001.

claim: Anxiety and stressful psychological life events strengthen visceral sensitivity.
source: Anxiety and stressful psychological life events lead to central nervous system (CNS) disorder triggering in turn gut motility dysfunctions (Mönnikes et al., 2001) and strengthen visceral sensitivity (Greenwood-Van Meerveld et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Greenwood-Van Meerveld et al., 2016.

claim: Stress animal models have been developed mimicking IBS features, such as changes in visceral sensitivity and gut transit time.
source: For a better understanding of the IBS pathophysiology, stress animal models have been developed mimicking IBS features, such as changes in visceral sensitivity and gut transit time (Gué et al., 1997).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Gué et al., 1997.

claim: Alternative probiotics were used to modulate visceral pain in IBS patients.
source: As an effective treatment, alternative probiotics were used to modulate visceral pain in IBS patients (Moayyedi et al., 2010; Hungin et al., 2013; Ford et al., 2014; Didari et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Moayyedi et al., 2010; Hungin et al., 2013; Ford et al., 2014; Didari et al., 2015.

claim: No consensus results were obtained from human clinical studies on probiotics for IBS.
source: However, no consensus results were obtained from human clinical studies (Mazurak et al., 2015) and mechanisms by which microbes signal from the gut lumen to the CNS, thus influencing pain perception, remain to be elucidated.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Mazurak et al., 2015.

claim: Mechanisms by which microbes signal from the gut lumen to the CNS, thus influencing pain perception, remain to be elucidated.
source: However, no consensus results were obtained from human clinical studies (Mazurak et al., 2015) and mechanisms by which microbes signal from the gut lumen to the CNS, thus influencing pain perception, remain to be elucidated.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Microbially produced neuroactive molecules can modulate the gut-brain axis communication.
source: In recent years, mounting evidence has suggested that microbially produced neuroactive molecules can modulate the gut-brain axis communication (Cryan and O'Mahony, 2011; Lyte, 2011; Reid, 2011; Cryan and Dinan, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Cryan and O'Mahony, 2011; Lyte, 2011; Reid, 2011; Cryan and Dinan, 2012.

claim: Ingestion of L. rhamnosus (JB-1) is able to regulate emotional behaviour and central γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA)ergic system in mouse via vagus nerve pathway.
source: For example, ingestion of a Lactobacillus strain, i.e., L. rhamnosus (JB-1) is able to regulate emotional behaviour and central γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA)ergic system in mouse via vagus nerve pathway (Bravo et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bravo et al., 2011.

claim: GABA-modulating bacteria of the human gut microbiota have been associated to brain signatures related to depression.
source: Recently, GABA-modulating bacteria of the human gut microbiota have been associated to brain signatures related to depression (Strandwitz et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Strandwitz et al., 2019.

claim: GABA is the main inhibitory CNS neurotransmitter in mammals.
source: In fact, GABA is the main inhibitory CNS neurotransmitter in mammals (Wong et al., 2003), and several important physiological functions have been characterized, such as neurotransmission, relaxing, and tranquilizer effects (Hayakawa et al., 2007; Li and Cao, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Wong et al., 2003.

claim: GABA has several important physiological functions including neurotransmission, relaxing, and tranquilizer effects.
source: In fact, GABA is the main inhibitory CNS neurotransmitter in mammals (Wong et al., 2003), and several important physiological functions have been characterized, such as neurotransmission, relaxing, and tranquilizer effects (Hayakawa et al., 2007; Li and Cao, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hayakawa et al., 2007; Li and Cao, 2010.

claim: GABA exerts its major functional effects via two GABA receptor subtypes, i.e., GABAA and GABAB.
source: GABA exerts these major functional effects via two GABA receptor subtypes, i.e., GABAA and GABAB (Hyland and Cryan, 2010) doing these receptors important pharmacological targets for clinically relevant anti-anxiety agents (Foster and Kemp, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hyland and Cryan, 2010.

claim: GABA receptors are important pharmacological targets for clinically relevant anti-anxiety agents.
source: GABA exerts these major functional effects via two GABA receptor subtypes, i.e., GABAA and GABAB (Hyland and Cryan, 2010) doing these receptors important pharmacological targets for clinically relevant anti-anxiety agents (Foster and Kemp, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Foster and Kemp, 2006.

claim: Glutamate constitutes up to 8–10% of amino acids in the human diet.
source: In the human diet, glutamate constitutes up to 8–10% of amino acids; it is involved in gut protein metabolism and is the precursor of different important molecules produced within the intestinal mucosa, like GABA.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about dietary composition.

claim: Glutamate is involved in gut protein metabolism and is the precursor of different important molecules produced within the intestinal mucosa, like GABA.
source: In the human diet, glutamate constitutes up to 8–10% of amino acids; it is involved in gut protein metabolism and is the precursor of different important molecules produced within the intestinal mucosa, like GABA.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about glutamate metabolism.

claim: GABA is synthetized by a pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (PLP)-dependent enzyme glutamate decarboxylase (GAD; EC 4.1.1.15) by irreversible α-decarboxylation of L-glutamate and consumption of one cytoplasmic proton.
source: GABA is synthetized by a pyridoxal-5'-phosphate (PLP)-dependent enzyme glutamate decarboxylase (GAD; EC 4.1.1.15) by irreversible α-decarboxylation of L-glutamate and consumption of one cytoplasmic proton (Ueno, 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ueno, 2000.

claim: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells are able to synthesize GABA, through the decarboxylation of glutamate.
source: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells are able to synthesize GABA, through the decarboxylation of glutamate and genes encoding GAD are present in the gut microbiota (Mazzoli and Pessione, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Mazzoli and Pessione, 2016.

claim: Genes encoding GAD are present in the gut microbiota.
source: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells are able to synthesize GABA, through the decarboxylation of glutamate and genes encoding GAD are present in the gut microbiota (Mazzoli and Pessione, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Mazzoli and Pessione, 2016.

claim: Glutamate import and GABA export generally occur in bacteria simultaneously via a specific glutamate/γ-amino butyrate antiporter.
source: Glutamate import and GABA export generally occur in bacteria simultaneously via a specific glutamate/γ-amino butyrate antiporter (Ma et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Ma et al., 2012.

claim: The glutamate-dependent system is associated with acid resistance in many bacteria.
source: The glutamate-dependent system is associated with acid resistance in many bacteria (Feehily and Karatzas, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Feehily and Karatzas, 2013.

claim: GABA has been classified as a health-promoting bioactive component in foods and pharmaceuticals.
source: Due to this large repertoire of beneficial effects, GABA has been classified as a health-promoting bioactive component in foods and pharmaceuticals (Li and Cao, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Li and Cao, 2010.

claim: Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) are generally recognized as safe sources to produce GABA at high levels and in an eco-friendly way.
source: Among bacteria, lactic acid bacteria (LAB) are generally recognized as safe sources to produce GABA at high levels and in an eco-friendly way (Dhakal et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dhakal et al., 2012.

claim: Food-derived lactobacilli and gut-derived Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium species are able to produce GABA in vitro.
source: Numerous studies revealed that food-derived lactobacilli and gut-derived Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium species are able to produce GABA in vitro (Li and Cao, 2010; Yunes et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Li and Cao, 2010; Yunes et al., 2016.

claim: A novel Streptococcus thermophilus strain was used for the production of a naturally GABA-enriched yogurt.
source: Interestingly, Linares et al., 2016 reported the use of a novel Streptococcus thermophilus strain for the production of a naturally GABA-enriched yogurt.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Linares et al., 2016.

claim: The link between bacterial GABA production in vitro and neuromodulatory activity in vivo remains poorly investigated.
source: However, the link between bacterial GABA production in vitro and neuromodulatory activity in vivo remains poorly investigated.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The human gut commensal GABA-producing Bifidobacterium dentium was shown in vivo to modulate sensory neuron activity in a rat faecal retention model of visceral hypersensitivity.
source: To date, only the human gut commensal GABA-producing Bifidobacterium dentium was shown in vivo to modulate sensory neuron activity in a rat faecal retention model of visceral hypersensitivity (Pokusaeva et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Pokusaeva et al., 2017.

claim: L. lactis is one of the most ingested bacteria.
source: Frequently encountered in dairy products, L. lactis is one of the most ingested bacteria (Mills et al., 2010; Laroute et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Mills et al., 2010; Laroute et al., 2017.

claim: L. lactis was found to persist transiently in the gut, depending on the strain under study.
source: Although not considered as a commensal bacterium, L. lactis was found to persist transiently in the gut, depending on the strain under study (Wang et al., 2011; Radziwill-Bienkowska et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2011; Radziwill-Bienkowska et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2016.

claim: L. lactis may exert in vivo a potent anti-inflammatory activity attenuating colitis.
source: It was also demonstrated that L. lactis may exert in vivo a potent anti-inflammatory activity attenuating colitis (Nishitani et al., 2009; Luerce et al., 2014; Ballal et al., 2015; Berlec et al., 2017; Nomura et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Nishitani et al., 2009; Luerce et al., 2014; Ballal et al., 2015; Berlec et al., 2017; Nomura et al., 1999.

claim: L. lactis is able to produce GABA in vitro.
source: L. lactis is also able to produce GABA in vitro (Nomura et al., 1999) and the well-characterized NCDO2118 strain besides its probiotic properties (Cordeiro et al., 2021), is considered as an efficient GABA producer among the species (Oliveira et al., 2017; Mazzoli et al., 2010; Oliveira et al., 2014; Laroute et al., 2016; Laroute et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Nomura et al., 1999.

claim: L. lactis NCDO2118 strain has probiotic properties.
source: L. lactis is also able to produce GABA in vitro (Nomura et al., 1999) and the well-characterized NCDO2118 strain besides its probiotic properties (Cordeiro et al., 2021), is considered as an efficient GABA producer among the species (Oliveira et al., 2017; Mazzoli et al., 2010; Oliveira et al., 2014; Laroute et al., 2016; Laroute et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Cordeiro et al., 2021.

claim: L. lactis NCDO2118 strain is considered as an efficient GABA producer among the species.
source: L. lactis is also able to produce GABA in vitro (Nomura et al., 1999) and the well-characterized NCDO2118 strain besides its probiotic properties (Cordeiro et al., 2021), is considered as an efficient GABA producer among the species (Oliveira et al., 2017; Mazzoli et al., 2010; Oliveira et al., 2014; Laroute et al., 2016; Laroute et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Oliveira et al., 2017; Mazzoli et al., 2010; Oliveira et al., 2014; Laroute et al., 2016; Laroute et al., 2021.

claim: The NCDO2118 strain was previously demonstrated to produce GABA in chemically defined medium.
source: The NCDO2118 strain previously demonstrated to produce GABA in chemically defined medium (Laroute et al., 2016), was grown in batch bioreactor with complex medium allowing high production of biomass and GABA (see Experimental section).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Laroute et al., 2016.

claim: The maximal concentrations of GABA and biomass reached, respectively, 40 mM at 24 hr and around 2.0 g/L at 8 hr for L. lactis NCDO2118 grown in complex medium.
source: In these conditions, the maximal concentrations of GABA and biomass reached, respectively, 40 mM at 24 hr and around 2.0 g/L at 8 hr, which are higher than the previously reported values in chemically defined medium (Laroute et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript and comparison to previous work.

claim: The maximal concentrations of GABA and biomass for L. lactis NCDO2118 in complex medium are higher than the previously reported values in chemically defined medium.
source: In these conditions, the maximal concentrations of GABA and biomass reached, respectively, 40 mM at 24 hr and around 2.0 g/L at 8 hr, which are higher than the previously reported values in chemically defined medium (Laroute et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of experimental data to previous work cited.

claim: The NCDO2727 strain has the gad operon involved in GABA biosynthesis similar to NCDO2118, in terms of genetic organization (gene sequences and promoter).
source: The NCDO2727 strain was demonstrated here to have the gad operon involved in GABA biosynthesis similar to NCDO2118, in terms of genetic organization (gene sequences and promoter).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from genetic analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: gadR, gadC, and gadB, the three genes of the gad operon are located between kefA and rnhB like in the NCDO2118 strain.
source: gadR, gadC, and gadB, the three genes of the gad operon are located between kefA and rnhB like in the NCDO2118 strain and the sequences of the corresponding proteins, GadR, C, and B, are highly similar with more than 99% of identity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from genetic analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: The sequences of the proteins GadR, C, and B in NCDO2727 are highly similar to NCDO2118 with more than 99% of identity.
source: gadR, gadC, and gadB, the three genes of the gad operon are located between kefA and rnhB like in the NCDO2118 strain and the sequences of the corresponding proteins, GadR, C, and B, are highly similar with more than 99% of identity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from genetic analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: Only two single nucleotide polymorphisms and a deletion of one bp were identified in the gadR and gadCB promoters, respectively, compared to NCDO2118.
source: Only two single nucleotide polymorphisms and a deletion of one bp were identified in the gadR and gadCB promoters, respectively, compared to NCDO2118.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from genetic analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: When tested for its GABA-producing performances under similar culture conditions, NCDO2727 GABA production was very weak (GABA concentration <0.2 mM).
source: However, when tested for its GABA-producing performances under similar culture conditions, GABA production was very weak (GABA concentration <0.2 mM, Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1.

claim: The biomass production of NCDO2727 was lower (maximal biomass around 0.5 g/L at 24 hr) than for the NCDO2118 strain.
source: The biomass production was lower (maximal biomass around 0.5 g/L at 24 hr) than for the NCDO2118 strain (Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 1.

claim: A high intracellular GAD activity was obtained at 7 hr in the NCDO2118 strain (45.3 ± 4.7 µmol/min.mg).
source: Interestingly, a high intracellular GAD activity was obtained at 7 hr in the NCDO2118 strain (45.3 ± 4.7 µmol/min.mg) consistently with its high GABA production ability, while in the NCDO2727 strain, no activity was detected.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from GAD activity measurements.

claim: In the NCDO2727 strain, no GAD activity was detected at 7 hr.
source: Interestingly, a high intracellular GAD activity was obtained at 7 hr in the NCDO2118 strain (45.3 ± 4.7 µmol/min.mg) consistently with its high GABA production ability, while in the NCDO2727 strain, no activity was detected.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from GAD activity measurements.

claim: The difference of GAD activity between the two strains was confirmed at 24 hr of culture.
source: The difference of GAD activity between the two strains was confirmed at 24 hr of culture (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Supplementary file 1.

claim: In vitro GABA production could not be solely associated to GABA genetic determinants in L. lactis.
source: This comparison demonstrated that in vitro GABA production could not be solely associated to GABA genetic determinants in L. lactis.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of NCDO2118 and NCDO2727 strains which have similar genetic determinants but different GABA production.

claim: GABA-producing L. lactis NCDO2118 in presence of glutamate had no impact on basal CRD sensitivity.
source: We first verified that GABA-producing L. lactis NCDO2118 in presence of glutamate had no impact on basal CRD sensitivity (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: In vehicle-treated rats, a 2 hr of partial restraint stress (PRS) significantly increased the number of abdominal contractions compared to basal conditions for all the pressures of distention applied from 30 mmHg (p<0.001).
source: Then, in vehicle-treated rats, a 2 hr of partial restraint stress (PRS) significantly increased the number of abdominal contractions compared to basal conditions for all the pressures of distention applied from 30 mmHg (p<0.001, Figure 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2.

claim: In presence of glutamate, oral administration of L. lactis NCDO2118 suppressed the PRS-induced enhancement of abdominal contractions (p<0.01 for all CRD pressures applied), restoring a quasi-basal sensitivity to CRD.
source: In presence of glutamate, oral administration of L. lactis NCDO2118 suppressed the PRS-induced enhancement of abdominal contractions (p<0.01 for all CRD pressures applied, Figure 2A), restoring a quasi-basal sensitivity to CRD.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2A.

claim: In absence of glutamate, the NCDO2118 strain did not exert antinociceptive properties.
source: However, in absence of glutamate, the NCDO2118 strain did not exert antinociceptive properties (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2A.

claim: Glutamate alone, at the concentration used (0.2% [w/v]), had no impact on basal CRD sensitivity and on visceral hypersensitivity response.
source: Glutamate alone, at the concentration used (0.2% [w/v]), had no impact on basal CRD sensitivity and on visceral hypersensitivity response (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Oral administration of the low GABA-producing L. lactis NCDO2727 in presence of glutamate failed to reduce stress-induced visceral hypersensitivity.
source: Oral administration of the low GABA-producing L. lactis NCDO2727 in presence of glutamate failed to reduce stress-induced visceral hypersensitivity (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 2B.

claim: The growth of the NCDO2118 ΔgadB mutant strain was close to that of the NCDO2118 strain under same culture conditions.
source: The growth of the NCDO2118 ΔgadB mutant strain, in which GABA pathway was interrupted (see Experimental section for strain construction details), was close to that of the NCDO2118 strain under same culture conditions (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The NCDO2118 ΔgadB mutant strain did not produce GABA (GABA concentration in the bioreactor <0.3 mM).
source: However, this strain did not produce GABA (GABA concentration in the bioreactor <0.3 mM Figure 3—figure supplement 1) and had no detectable GAD activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The NCDO2118 ΔgadB mutant strain had no detectable GAD activity.
source: However, this strain did not produce GABA (GABA concentration in the bioreactor <0.3 mM Figure 3—figure supplement 1) and had no detectable GAD activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from GAD activity measurements.

claim: There was no impact of the NCDO2118 ΔgadB mutant strain on the visceral hypersensitivity response induced by stress in response to CRD in presence of glutamate.
source: There was no impact of this strain on the visceral hypersensitivity response induced by stress in response to CRD in presence of glutamate (Figure 3A, p<0.05 NCDO2118 ΔgadB- vs. NCDO2118-treated animals).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 3A.

claim: The beneficial effect of L. lactis NCDO2118 treatment on stress-induced visceral hypersensitivity (P<0.05) was completely abolished when animals received the GABAB receptor antagonist SCH-50911 in presence of glutamate.
source: The beneficial effect of L. lactis NCDO2118 treatment on stress-induced visceral hypersensitivity (P<0.05) was completely abolished when animals received the GABAB receptor antagonist SCH-50911 in presence of glutamate (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 3B.

claim: For the NCDO2118 strain, the GABA level was high in the stomach and then tended to decrease in the other gut compartments (p<0.05 in caecum vs stomach).
source: For the NCDO2118 strain, the GABA level was high in the stomach and then tended to decrease in the other gut compartments (p<0.05 in caecum vs stomach; Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4A.

claim: In vehicle- or NCDO2727-treated animals, the GABA levels were similar all along the gastro-intestinal tract.
source: In contrast, in vehicle- or NCDO2727-treated animals, the GABA levels were similar all along the gastro-intestinal tract (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4B.

claim: In the stomach, the GABA production by L. lactis NCDO2118 was higher than that measured in vehicle or NCDO2727 strain.
source: Consistently, in the stomach, the GABA production by L. lactis NCDO2118 was higher than that measured in vehicle or NCDO2727 strain (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4C.

claim: In rat gastric juice, the rate of GABA production by the NCDO2727 strain was similar to the vehicle.
source: In particular in rat gastric juice, we found that the rate of GABA production by the NCDO2727 strain was similar to the vehicle but the rate of GABA production by the NCDO2118 strain was fourfold increased (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Supplementary file 2.

claim: In rat gastric juice, the rate of GABA production by the NCDO2118 strain was fourfold increased compared to vehicle.
source: In particular in rat gastric juice, we found that the rate of GABA production by the NCDO2727 strain was similar to the vehicle but the rate of GABA production by the NCDO2118 strain was fourfold increased (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Supplementary file 2.

claim: The composition of the faecal microbiota was not globally impacted by the L. lactis NCDO2118 treatment.
source: The composition of the faecal microbiota was not globally impacted by the L. lactis NCDO2118 treatment (Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 5.

claim: No changes in α and β diversities were observed after L. lactis NCDO2118 treatment.
source: Particularly, no changes in α and β diversities were observed (Figure 5A and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 5A and C.

claim: The non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis test on each of the 150 identified genera present in samples revealed few differences in taxon abundances in faecal microbiota, in particular significantly for three genera, Clostridium (p=0.023), Frisingicoccus, and Papillibacter (p=0.041), and nearly significantly for Escherichia genus (p=0.069), after L. lactis NCDO2118 treatment.
source: Besides, the non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis test on each of the 150 identified genera present in samples revealed few differences in taxon abundances in faecal microbiota, in particular significantly for three genera, Clostridium (p=0.023), Frisingicoccus, and Papillibacter (p=0.041), and nearly significantly for Escherichia genus (p=0.069), after L. lactis NCDO2118 treatment (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Supplementary file 3.

claim: A transient food-borne LAB L. lactis (strain NCDO2118) exerts, in an animal model of acute stress, visceral anti-hypersensitivity effects via its ability to produce significant levels of GABA in vivo.
source: For the first time, we demonstrated that a transient food-borne LAB L. lactis (strain NCDO2118) exerts, in an animal model of acute stress, visceral anti-hypersensitivity effects via its ability to produce significant levels of GABA in vivo, due to an active GAD enzymatic potential and not solely to the presence of gadB gene.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The visceral anti-hypersensitivity effects of L. lactis NCDO2118 are due to an active GAD enzymatic potential and not solely to the presence of gadB gene.
source: For the first time, we demonstrated that a transient food-borne LAB L. lactis (strain NCDO2118) exerts, in an animal model of acute stress, visceral anti-hypersensitivity effects via its ability to produce significant levels of GABA in vivo, due to an active GAD enzymatic potential and not solely to the presence of gadB gene.
evidence: This claim is supported by the comparison of NCDO2118 and NCDO2727 strains which have similar genetic determinants but different GAD activity and in vivo effects.

claim: The low GABA producer NCDO2727 strain fails to exert antinociceptive effect.
source: Indeed, the low GABA producer NCDO2727 strain and NCDO2118 ΔgadB mutant strain unable to produce GABA, fail to exert such antinociceptive effect.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: NCDO2118 ΔgadB mutant strain unable to produce GABA fails to exert antinociceptive effect.
source: Indeed, the low GABA producer NCDO2727 strain and NCDO2118 ΔgadB mutant strain unable to produce GABA, fail to exert such antinociceptive effect.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The antinociceptive effect of L. lactis NCDO2118 is mediated by the metabolically active NCDO2118 which delivers GABA in the gastro-intestinal tract, that in turn influences host GABAergic host physiological system.
source: This effect is mediated by the metabolically active NCDO2118 which delivers GABA in the gastro-intestinal tract, that in turn influences host GABAergic host physiological system.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing GABA production in vivo and the blocking of the effect by GABAB receptor antagonist.

claim: L. lactis is a very common bacterium widely used in food industry with a GRAS status.
source: L. lactis is a very common bacterium widely used in food industry with a GRAS status.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about L. lactis.

claim: Genes encoding GAD are found in numerous bacteria present in different environments and ecosystems, i.e., native soil, natural landscape as well as in the gastro-intestinal tract.
source: Even though genes encoding GAD are found in numerous bacteria present in different environments and ecosystems, i.e., native soil, natural landscape as well as in the gastro-intestinal tract, the ability of these bacteria to produce GABA has not systematically been evidenced.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about GAD genes in bacteria.

claim: The ability of bacteria with GAD genes to produce GABA has not systematically been evidenced.
source: Even though genes encoding GAD are found in numerous bacteria present in different environments and ecosystems, i.e., native soil, natural landscape as well as in the gastro-intestinal tract, the ability of these bacteria to produce GABA has not systematically been evidenced.
evidence: This is stated as a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: Only a 10-day chronic oral administration of the high producer NCDO2118 strain displaying a high GAD activity is able to reduce visceral hypersensitivity induced by stress.
source: Herein, we demonstrate in vivo that only a 10-day chronic oral administration of the high producer NCDO2118 strain displaying a high GAD activity is able to reduce visceral hypersensitivity induced by stress.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The antinociceptive effect of NCDO2118 was accompanied by an increased GABA production in the gastric compartment.
source: This effect was accompanied by an increased GABA production in the gastric compartment.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Transient NCDO2118 strain is metabolically active in vivo to deliver GABA in the gastro-intestinal tract lumen.
source: Taken together, all these observations suggest that transient NCDO2118 strain is metabolically active in vivo to deliver GABA in the gastro-intestinal tract lumen.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing GABA production in vivo.

claim: The NCDO2118 treatment did not shift the overall diversity of the faecal microbiota.
source: We evaluated the impact of the NCDO2118 treatment on the faecal microbiota and observed no changes in α or β diversity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Probiotic treatment did not shift the overall diversity of the intestinal microbiota of mice, rats, or humans in many other studies on IBS.
source: This result is consistent with observations in many other studies on IBS that have shown that probiotic treatment did not shift the overall diversity of the intestinal microbiota of mice, rats, or humans (Cussotto et al., 2021; Grazul et al., 2016; Jeffery et al., 2020; Labus et al., 2017; Tap et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Cussotto et al., 2021; Grazul et al., 2016; Jeffery et al., 2020; Labus et al., 2017; Tap et al., 2017.

claim: In 'healthy microbiota' the addition of a probiotic does not promptly impact the resident microbial populations but rather could have a significant impact on reshaping the microbiota in an already existing dysbiosis.
source: Indeed, in 'healthy microbiota' the addition of a probiotic does not promptly impact the resident microbial populations but rather could have a significant impact on reshaping the microbiota in an already existing dysbiosis humans (Alander et al., 1999; Eloe-Fadrosh et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Alander et al., 1999; Eloe-Fadrosh et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2004.

claim: An enrichment of the Clostridium genus was found after L. lactis NCDO2118 treatment compared to the vehicle group.
source: We next compared genera abundancies after treatment using non-parametric tests and found an enrichment of the Clostridium genus after L. lactis NCDO2118 treatment compared to the vehicle group.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from microbiota analysis.

claim: The Clostridium genus was shown in silico as modulating GABA (i.e. GABA producer and consumer) in humans.
source: This genus was shown in silico as modulating GABA (i.e. GABA producer and consumer) in humans (Strandwitz et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Strandwitz et al., 2019.

claim: An enrichment of the Escherichia genus was observed after L. lactis NCDO2118 treatment.
source: An enrichment of the Escherichia genus was also observed.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from microbiota analysis.

claim: In the study on the E. coli Nissle 1917 strain, GABA was not able to directly cross the epithelial barrier, requiring the C12AsnGABAOH lipopeptide for functionalization and subsequent translocation.
source: Interestingly, in the study on the E. coli Nissle 1917 strain, Pérez-Berezo and colleagues showed that GABA was not able to directly cross the epithelial barrier (Pérez-Berezo et al., 2017), requiring the C12AsnGABAOH lipopeptide for functionalization and subsequent translocation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Pérez-Berezo et al., 2017.

claim: The enrichment of the genus Escherichia in the faecal microbiota of L. lactis-treated animals could help reduce visceral pain via a lipopeptide-mediated GABA functionalization pathway.
source: It is then possible that the enrichment of the genus Escherichia in the faecal microbiota of L. lactis-treated animals could help reduce visceral pain via a lipopeptide-mediated GABA functionalization pathway.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on inference from previous work.

claim: C12AsnGABAOH lipopeptide was not detected in L. lactis NCDO2118.
source: Of note, in our study, using the same method as previously described (Pérez-Berezo et al., 2017), we were not able to detect any C12AsnGABAOH lipopeptide in L. lactis NCDO2118 (results not shown).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the study.

claim: GABA is the major inhibitory neuromediator, mainly involved in regulating physiological and psychological responses.
source: GABA is the major inhibitory neuromediator, mainly involved in regulating physiological and psychological responses.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about GABA.

claim: Indirect evidences point out the effect of gut microbiota as well as probiotic strains on CNS by modulating the GABAergic system.
source: Today, indirect evidences point out the effect of gut microbiota as well as probiotic strains (Cryan and Dinan, 2012) on CNS by modulating the GABAergic system.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Cryan and Dinan, 2012.

claim: Alterations of the GABAergic system have a key role in the development of stress-related psychiatric disorders.
source: Moreover, alterations of this GABAergic system have a key role in the development of stress-related psychiatric disorders (Schür et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Schür et al., 2016.

claim: The involvement of GABAB receptor in the visceral antinociceptive effect mediated by the delivery of GABA produced by the NCDO2118 strain was demonstrated using a specific antagonist (SCH-50911).
source: Using a specific antagonist (SCH-50911), we demonstrated the involvement of GABAB receptor in the visceral antinociceptive effect mediated by the delivery of GABA produced by the NCDO2118 strain.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: GABAB receptors are strongly expressed in the gastro-intestinal tract.
source: GABAB receptors are strongly expressed in the gastro-intestinal tract (Hyland and Cryan, 2010) and widely distributed from the stomach to the ileum in the enteric nervous system (ENS; Auteri et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hyland and Cryan, 2010.

claim: GABAB receptors are widely distributed from the stomach to the ileum in the enteric nervous system (ENS).
source: GABAB receptors are strongly expressed in the gastro-intestinal tract (Hyland and Cryan, 2010) and widely distributed from the stomach to the ileum in the enteric nervous system (ENS; Auteri et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Auteri et al., 2015.

claim: Previous studies established the presence of autocrine and paracrine GABA signalling mechanisms in gastro-intestinal epithelial cells via GABA receptor activation in rodents.
source: In rodents, previous studies established the presence of autocrine and paracrine GABA signalling mechanisms in gastro-intestinal epithelial cells via GABA receptor activation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: In rat, GABAB receptors have been identified on the mucosal gland cells of the stomach.
source: In rat, GABAB receptors have also been identified on the mucosal gland cells of the stomach (Castelli et al., 1999; Erdo and Bowery, 1986; Erdö et al., 1990; Krantis et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Castelli et al., 1999; Erdo and Bowery, 1986; Erdö et al., 1990; Krantis et al., 1994.

claim: The GABAB metabotropic receptors in the gastro-intestinal tract are known to regulate several gut functions and gut-to-brain signalling pathway.
source: Actually, the GABAB metabotropic receptors in the gastro-intestinal tract are known to regulate several gut functions and gut-to-brain signalling pathway (Hyland and Cryan, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hyland and Cryan, 2010.

claim: In mice, selective stimulation of GABAB receptors increases gastric acid secretion both through vagal cholinergic and gastrin-dependent mechanisms.
source: In mice, selective stimulation of GABAB receptors increases gastric acid secretion both through vagal cholinergic and gastrin-dependent mechanisms (Piqueras and Martinez, 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Piqueras and Martinez, 2004.

claim: Combined central and peripheral mechanisms result in an increase in the luminal acidity, which provides a supportive environment for the GAD activity of L. lactis NCDO2118.
source: These combined central and peripheral mechanisms result in an increase in the luminal acidity, which provides a supportive environment for the GAD activity of L. lactis NCDO2118.
evidence: This is inferred from the previous claim about GABAB receptor stimulation increasing gastric acid secretion.

claim: A significant level of GABA production was measured after 10-day administration of L. lactis NCDO2118 in the stomach.
source: Accordingly, and despite a limited number of animals, we observed herein a significant level of GABA production measured after 10-day administration of L. lactis NCDO2118 in the stomach, which was supported by an in vitro GABA production in gastric juice sampled from naive rats and supplemented with glutamate; in this way, a dynamic 'virtuous circle' would be generated between L. lactis NCDO2118 and the host.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In vitro GABA production in gastric juice sampled from naive rats and supplemented with glutamate supports the in vivo GABA production in the stomach.
source: Accordingly, and despite a limited number of animals, we observed herein a significant level of GABA production measured after 10-day administration of L. lactis NCDO2118 in the stomach, which was supported by an in vitro GABA production in gastric juice sampled from naive rats and supplemented with glutamate; in this way, a dynamic 'virtuous circle' would be generated between L. lactis NCDO2118 and the host.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A dynamic 'virtuous circle' would be generated between L. lactis NCDO2118 and the host.
source: Accordingly, and despite a limited number of animals, we observed herein a significant level of GABA production measured after 10-day administration of L. lactis NCDO2118 in the stomach, which was supported by an in vitro GABA production in gastric juice sampled from naive rats and supplemented with glutamate; in this way, a dynamic 'virtuous circle' would be generated between L. lactis NCDO2118 and the host.
evidence: This is a speculative claim inferred from the experimental data.

claim: Vagal and splanchnic afferents of GABAB receptors are involved in the modulation of sensitivity.
source: Furthermore, vagal and splanchnic afferents of GABAB receptors are involved in the modulation of sensitivity (Hyland and Cryan, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Hyland and Cryan, 2010.

claim: Probiotic strains have been described to modulate brain functions via a dependent vagus activation pathway.
source: Probiotic strains have been described to modulate brain functions via a dependent vagus activation pathway (Bravo et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bravo et al., 2011.

claim: The Bravo et al. 2011 study was the first to demonstrate the ability of Lactobacillus to modify central levels of GABA through the stimulation of the vagus nerve.
source: This study was the first to demonstrate the ability of Lactobacillus to modify central levels of GABA through the stimulation of the vagus nerve.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Bravo et al., 2011.

claim: Central GABA release goes hand with beneficial effect on emotional behaviour impairments induced by stress.
source: This central GABA release goes hand with beneficial effect on emotional behaviour impairments induced by stress.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the Bravo et al. 2011 study.

claim: The primary molecular mechanisms underlying how Lactobacillus stimulated vagal afferents were not resolved in the Bravo et al. 2011 study.
source: However, the primary molecular mechanisms underlying how Lactobacillus stimulated vagal afferents were not resolved.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the Bravo et al. 2011 study.

claim: A neurotransmitter, i.e., GABA, directly produced by L. lactis NCDO2118 into the gastro-intestinal tract lumen, exerted beneficial effect on stress-induced gut visceral hypersensitivity via GABAB receptor stimulation.
source: Here, we could firmly demonstrate that a neurotransmitter, i.e., GABA, directly produced by L. lactis NCDO2118 into the gastro-intestinal tract lumen, exerted beneficial effect on stress-induced gut visceral hypersensitivity via GABAB receptor stimulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: According to its ability to deliver into the gastro-intestinal tract lumen neurometabolites like GABA in significant levels, L. lactis NCDO2118 could be considered as a helpful candidate in the management of functional gastro-intestinal disorders associated with stressful situations.
source: In conclusion, our data strongly suggest that, according to its ability to deliver into the gastro-intestinal tract lumen neurometabolites like GABA in significant levels, L. lactis NCDO2118 could be considered as a helpful candidate in the management of functional gastro-intestinal disorders associated with stressful situations.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: GAD activity rather than genetic organization of gad genes appears as a key determinant for in vivo antinociceptive properties of L. lactis.
source: Regarding our results, GAD activity rather than genetic organization of gad genes appears as a key determinant for in vivo antinociceptive properties of L. lactis.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data comparing NCDO2118 and NCDO2727 strains.

claim: This work opens perspectives for GRAS L. lactis strains as future therapeutic agents for the management of visceral pain and the anxious profile of IBS patients.
source: Therefore, this work opens perspectives for GRAS L. lactis strains as future therapeutic agents for the management of visceral pain and the anxious profile of IBS patients.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about future applications based on the experimental data.

claim: L. lactis NCDO2118 ΔgadB mutant was constructed by double crossing over in the chromosome.
source: L. lactis NCDO2118 ΔgadB mutant was constructed by double crossing over in the chromosome as previously described (Maguin et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Maguin et al., 1996 and describes the experimental method.
